name: Ariva: delivery from Azure DevOps
description: The move of Ariva's delivery to Azure DevOps and Dalil's Azure (owner request 2026-10-20; the plan is docs/plan/azure-devops-move.md). Today GitHub Actions is the gate and the dev release, and the Azure DevOps pipelines in Platform/Cloud/Ariva.Cicd/AzureDevOps exist but have never run: the pull request pipeline would fail as written, the image builds are unscanned and unsigned, and the release deploys a mutable tag without approval or signature checks. These stories bring the Azure pipelines to the GitHub ones' level, then cut over. Option A (GitHub stays the code's home, Azure Pipelines delivers) or Option B (Azure Repos becomes the home) is the owner's first decision; the stories say where they differ. Agents never run releases or change clusters; the steps in Azure DevOps and Azure are the owner's.

userStories.title: [E0] Azure DevOps project and repository setup
userStories.description: Owner steps in Azure DevOps, with the agent writing the checklist: the project, the connection to the code (Option A: the Azure Pipelines GitHub app on alsadderwork-coder/Ariva; Option B: Azure Repos import with every branch and the full history), and for Option B the branch policies on main that replace the GitHub ruleset and CODEOWNERS.
acceptanceCriteria: The owner records decision 1 of docs/plan/azure-devops-move.md (Option A or B) in docs/product/decisions.md and an ADR-0016 amendment (Proposed until accepted)

docs/harness/azure-devops.md lists every setting the owner makes, step by step: the project, the code connection, and for Option B the import, the default branch, the build validation policy (Analyze-solution), reviewers, path-based required reviewers mirroring .github/CODEOWNERS, the merge type limited to rebase and fast-forward, force push and delete denied on main and v* tags
The owner confirms each step done; the story passes on that record (agents cannot change Azure DevOps settings)

userStories.title: [E17] Azure pull request gate at the GitHub gate's level
userStories.description: Common/Analyze-solution.yaml would fail as written: it starts only PostgreSQL while the E2E configuration needs Kafka and Redis in CI, and it lacks the docs rules, the base image check, chart security with Helm and Helmfile, the offline bundle self-tests and dry run, the TLS check self-test, the vulnerable package list, the AsyncAPI validation and the test-count check that ci.yml runs. Its header still says trunk.
acceptanceCriteria: Analyze-solution.yaml runs every check ci.yml runs (or names each one it leaves out and why), with Kafka and Redis beside PostgreSQL pinned by the same digests, the same artifact secret check before anything is published, and main instead of trunk
A check (in scripts/base-images.mjs or its own script, self-tested) compares the two gates' step lists and fails when ci.yml gains a check the Azure gate lacks
A run on Azure DevOps passes on the branch (run by the owner; its result recorded in backlog/progress.md)
node scripts/verify.mjs quick passes, and node scripts/security/scan.mjs passes with 0 errors
security-reviewer verdict PASS recorded in backlog/progress.md
docs and wiki pages affected by the change are updated (node scripts/verify.mjs docs passes)
userStories.notes: Size M. 2026-10-25 (ARV-164a, ARV-164b): ci.yml runs both test suites as their executables (Microsoft Testing Platform) and then scripts/test-count-guard.mjs on each TRX; Analyze-solution's DotNetCoreCLI test task still runs them through dotnet test (VSTest), whose adapter can drop a case, a failing one included, without failing the run. Run the executables and the guard as ci.yml does. 2026-10-28 (ARV-252): ci.yml writes both suites' output to unit.log and integration.log, checks them and the TRX files with artifact-secrets.mjs before printing, quoting or uploading any of it (backendLogWiring holds the wiring); the Azure gate's logs are the project's own, not public, but its published test results are artifacts: check them the same way before they are published.

userStories.title: [E0] Azure image builds scanned, signed and with SBOMs
userStories.description: The Build-k8s-<service> pipelines build and push to dalil.azurecr.io/ariva without a scan, a signature or an SBOM, and their path filters miss files the Dockerfiles copy (scripts/published-runtime.mjs, GlobalSuppressions.cs).
acceptanceCriteria: Every image build has complete path filters (checked against each Dockerfile's COPY lines by scripts/base-images.mjs), a Trivy image scan that fails on high or critical findings with a fix, a CycloneDX SBOM, a signature and a signed SBOM attestation by the key of decision 2 (cosign with an Azure Key Vault key, or the documented alternative), and a digest table artifact as images.yml makes
wiki/04-Deployment-Guide.md section 6.5 gives the verification command for the Azure-signed images and the admission policy example for them
A build on Azure DevOps produces a signed image whose signature and SBOM verify (run by the owner; recorded in backlog/progress.md)

userStories.title: [E0] Azure dev release at the GitHub release's level
userStories.description: Release-ariva-k8s-dev.yaml installs an unpinned kubectl and unchecked Helm, Helmfile and helm-diff, writes appsettings from variables with echo, passes the registry password as a Helm value, deploys the mutable tag main with no signature check and has no approval. release-dev.yml does all of that properly and is the model.
acceptanceCriteria: The release runs as a deployment job on the k8s-dev environment (the owner's approval), from main only
Every tool is pinned by version and checksum as in release-dev.yml, and scripts/base-images.mjs holds the Azure release's tool versions to the GitHub ones

Every image's signature is verified and its digest passed as imageDigests, the pull secret is made out of band (ARV-209's first criterion), the one-time secrets are checked, and the TLS check and the pod evidence run after the release
The cluster is reached through a Kubernetes service connection scoped to the namespace, or the reason it stays a kubeconfig secret is recorded
The one-time switch between the GitHub and Azure releases (the dalilacr-secret delete) is in wiki 04 with both directions

userStories.title: [E19] Offline bundle signed and verified without GitHub's OIDC identity
userStories.description: scripts/offline/verify.mjs accepts only signatures by GitHub's OIDC issuer from this repository's workflows; with Option B, or with the Key Vault key of decision 2, the offline bundle needs a key-based identity.
acceptanceCriteria: The offline bundle pipeline signs the manifest with the decision 2 key in a job that runs no build or package manager (the rule of ARV-127), and verify.mjs accepts that key's identity and refuses any other
Its self-tests cover the key identity (a good bundle, a bundle signed by another key, a tampered file) and a rehearsal with real cosign passes
Where the signed bundle is archived (Dalil's release store) is recorded in wiki 04 section 12
